bull.t: Recurring EDA revenue and customer expansion
bull.b: Subscription-like EDA contracts, renewals and add-ons create durable revenue visibility. Broad adoption across customer workflows can increase wallet share and make Cadence's tools harder to replace over multiple design cycles.

bull.t: Strong demand, backlog and market expansion
bull.b: Record backlog and raised growth guidance indicate sustained customer commitments rather than isolated quarterly demand. Exposure to AI, advanced packaging, 3D IC and complex computing supports continued structural EDA spending.

Very high software margins and strong conversion of earnings into free cash flow provide resources for research, integration, debt management and shareholder returns. This supports resilience as Cadence invests in future product opportunities.

bear.b: Although leverage is not extreme and cash generation is strong, the materially higher debt burden reduces flexibility versus prior years. It could constrain investment or increase sensitivity to weaker semiconductor spending and integration execution.

Cadence serves global semiconductor and system customers, so regulatory changes could restrict sales, delay approvals or alter customer programs. Guidance dependence on stable rules makes international growth and forecasts vulnerable to policy shifts.

bear.t: Investment and integration pressure on margins
bear.b: Higher R&D, sales and integration spending is intended to capture future opportunities, but it can suppress near-term operating leverage. Returns depend on successful execution and monetization of new initiatives without weakening the core margin profile.
